variants.name: The Ma'rib Dam
variants.short: A monumental testament to the ingenuity of our forebears. With some slight flaws…
variants.flavour: The Ma'rib Dam - just outside the Sabaean city that shares its name - is one of, if not the oldest dam in the world. First constructed to catch rainwater during the monsoon to irrigate crops, the dam was modified in height and breadth over many centuries. However, this weakened the structure, leading to more frequent breaches that were more difficult to repair on each subsequent occasion. The dam has remained unrepaired since late in the 6th century AD; it is thought that the cost of repairs was too great following the collapse of the Himyarite Kingdom earlier in the century. This state of affairs led to the mass-migration of around 50,000 people who had been living in the Dhana Valley at the time, a great movement of people by the standards of the time, and something that even warranted a mention in the Quran.
